items.informal_name: Wronskian Equality for Polynomials with Sum Zero
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {a b c : Polynomial R}, a + b + c = 0 → a.wronskian b = b.wronskian c
items.informal_description: If three polynomials $a$, $b$, and $c$ satisfy $a + b + c = 0$, then their Wronskians satisfy $\mathrm{Wronskian}(a, b) = \mathrm{Wronskian}(b, c)$, where the Wronskian of two polynomials $f$ and $g$ is defined as $f \cdot g' - f' \cdot g$.

items.informal_name: Wronskian is additive in the first argument
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (a b c : Polynomial R), (a + b).wronskian c = a.wronskian c + b.wronskian c
items.informal_description: For any polynomials $a$, $b$, and $c$ over a commutative ring $R$, the Wronskian of $a + b$ and $c$ is equal to the sum of the Wronskians of $a$ and $c$ and of $b$ and $c$, i.e., $ \text{Wronskian}(a + b, c) = \text{Wronskian}(a, c) + \text{Wronskian}(b, c) $.

items.informal_name: Additivity of Wronskian in the Second Argument
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (a b c : Polynomial R), a.wronskian (b + c) = a.wronskian b + a.wronskian c
items.informal_description: For any polynomials $a, b, c$ over a commutative ring $R$, the Wronskian satisfies $\operatorname{Wronskian}(a, b + c) = \operatorname{Wronskian}(a, b) + \operatorname{Wronskian}(a, c)$, where the Wronskian is defined as $a \cdot b' - a' \cdot b$ with $'$ denoting the formal derivative.

items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (a b : Polynomial R), a.wronskian (-b) = -a.wronskian b
items.informal_description: For any polynomials $ a $ and $ b $ over a ring $ R $, the Wronskian of $ a $ and $ -b $ satisfies $ W(a, -b) = -W(a, b) $, where $ W(a, b) = a b' - a' b $ denotes the Wronskian of $ a $ and $ b $.

items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (a b : Polynomial R), (-a).wronskian b = -a.wronskian b
items.informal_description: For any polynomials $a$ and $b$ over a commutative ring $R$, the Wronskian of $-a$ and $b$ is equal to the negative of the Wronskian of $a$ and $b$, i.e., $\operatorname{Wronskian}(-a, b) = -\operatorname{Wronskian}(a, b)$.

items.type:
